title: An international multicentre registry collecting data on patients treated with SBRT for HCC (HepReg)
summary:
In this study, an international database will be established to collect information on the treatment of liver cancer with SBRT.
SBRT is a very precise form of radiation therapy that targets tumors accurately while sparing the surrounding healthy tissue as much as possible.

The main goal of the study is to find out how often serious side effects occur after SBRT treatment.
In addition, the study will examine how effective the treatment is, for example, how long patients live, how long the disease remains stable, and how well the tumor can be controlled locally.
The combination of SBRT with other medications commonly used in clinical practice will also be analyzed.

The data collection consists of two parts:
On the one hand, new patient data will be collected from October 2023 to October 2027 (prospective study).
On the other hand, existing data from patients who were treated in the past will also be evaluated (retrospective study).

In addition, data from patients who have died after treatment and can therefore no longer provide consent will also be included.

interventions.name: Retrospective and prospective collection of clinical patient data. Therapeutic interventions are not planned.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The following criteria apply to both the retrospective and the prospective registry study:
• Treatment of HCC with SBRT
• Female and male patients aged 18 years or older
• Informed consent of the patient by means of a written declaration of consent for the transmission of data to the registry (for the prospective teil)

All patients who have been treated in the past will be included in the retrospective analysis.
In the prospective analysis, patients receiving SBRT for HCC as part of routine medical care at one of the participating centers will be registered.
Exclusion criteria:
No exclusion criteria are defined for this registry.
Any patient who meets the above inclusion criteria may be registered.
